title: Space-valued Yoneda evaluation and density
statement:
Use the universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, coherent functors, spaces, mapping spaces and colimits of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] and [def-coef-presentable-infinity-category]; small means $\mathcal U$-small. Let $C$ be a small quasicategory, let $\mathcal S$ be the infinity category of small Kan complexes with their full coherent mapping spaces, and put $\mathcal P(C)=\operatorname{Fun}(C^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)$. The Yoneda functor is $h:C\to\mathcal P(C)$, $h_c=\operatorname{Map}_C(-,c)$. For every $c\in C$ and $F\in\mathcal P(C)$, evaluation at the identity of $c$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(h_c,F)\simeq F(c),$$
natural coherently in $c$ and $F$. Moreover, for every $F\in\mathcal P(C)$ there are a small simplicial set $E_F$, a coherent diagram $p_F:E_F\to C$, and a colimiting coherent cocone $h\circ p_F\to F$. Thus its apex satisfies $F\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{e\in E_F}h_{p_F(e)}$. The diagram and cocone retain all transformations and higher homotopies; the assertion concerns space-valued presheaves, not just their sets of components.

source.place: Lemma 5.1.5.2 (evaluation corepresented by Yoneda) and Lemma 5.1.5.3 (Yoneda density), printed pp. 321-323. The small model for the indexing diagram is the right fibration of elements of a small-space-valued functor on small C. Read online (March 10, 2012 text), not archived in literature/. No Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical result.

proof.text:
Use the right-fibration equivalence, including its full mapping-space and pullback comparisons, in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification]. Choose a small right fibration $p_F:E_F\to C$ classifying $F$; smallness of its total simplicial set is an explicit clause of that node because $C$ is small and every value of $F$ is a small space. The total simplicial set $E_F$ is a quasicategory: project any inner horn to $C$, fill it there, and lift the resulting simplex through $p_F$, since the right-fibration lifting range contains every inner horn. For any other presheaf $G$ choose $p_G:E_G\to C$ in the same way. The classification gives
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(F,G)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/C}(E_F,E_G).$$
These are Kan spaces, with the full simplicial mapping data specified there. The same node identifies $h_c$ with the right fibration $C_{/c}\to C$, coherently in $c$, and identifies its identity vertex with $1_c$. The slice is a small quasicategory and its projection is a right fibration by [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration]. The presheaf functor category is a quasicategory by [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus], so its mapping spaces and coherent cocones have the conventions required below.

source.place: Sections 2.2.1 and 5.1.1, and Lemma 5.1.5.2: use the existing coherent right-fibration model; agent expansion of the smallness and model choices.

proof.text:
The identity edge $1_c$ is an equivalence, so [lem-coef-infinity-slice-equivalence-final] makes it a final object of $C_{/c}$. Hence [lem-coef-infinity-terminal-anodyne] makes $\{1_c\}\hookrightarrow C_{/c}$ right anodyne. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to this inclusion and $p_F:E_F\to C$, and take the pullback over the fixed projection $C_{/c}\to C$. Its restriction map is a trivial Kan fibration
$$\operatorname{Fun}_{/C}(C_{/c},E_F)\longrightarrow (E_F)_c.$$
By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-homotopy-equivalence] it admits a simplicial homotopy inverse, so it is an equivalence of spaces. The identifications in step 1 identify it with $\tau\mapsto\tau_c(1_c)$, and identify its target with $F(c)$. This proves the evaluation equivalence. Its coherent naturality is checked in the same over-map model, rather than by selecting separate inverses at each vertex: for $u:c\to c'$ the functor $C_{/c}\to C_{/c'}$ is postcomposition by $u$, and the lift over $u$ into the value at $1_{c'}$ identifies the value at $u$ with $F(u)$ of that value. Thus precomposition by $h(u)$ corresponds to $F(u)$; postcomposition by $F\to G$ corresponds to the induced fiber map. The transport/composition/unit clause and pullback compatibility of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] supply these comparisons for simplices and their compositions. Restriction and the exponential map act on the entire parameter simplex $\Delta^n$, so these are comparisons of coherent bifunctors, including all higher homotopies.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4, with Corollary 4.7.3.22 (02J5) and Proposition 4.7.3.20 (02J2); the contravariant version of the proof of HTT Lemma 5.1.5.2. Kerodon identifiers are not Stacks tags.

proof.text:
Record a consequence of the classification that will compute the universal property, with its argument included here. Let $K$ be a small quasicategory, $H:K^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$, and $q:Q\to K$ its small right-fibration representative. Put $\Gamma=\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K,Q)$. The constant-point clause and mapping-space formula of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] show that $\Gamma$ is a small Kan complex. Evaluation of sections gives a coherent cone $\Delta_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}\Gamma\to H$. For every small Kan complex $T$, the Kan mapping-complex model and the degreewise exponential adjunction give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S}(T,\Gamma)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}(T,\Gamma)\cong\operatorname{Fun}_{/K}(K\times T,Q)\simeq\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(K^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(\Delta_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}T,H).$$
The first comparison is the same classification with base $\Delta^0$, where a Kan complex itself represents the classified space. The last comparison is precisely the cited classification applied to the constant functor with value $T$. The middle isomorphism sends $a:T\to\Gamma$ to $(k,t)\mapsto a(t)(k)$ in every simplicial degree; hence the displayed map is the map induced by the evaluation cone. The cone criterion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] now proves that this very cone is limiting, so $\Gamma\simeq\lim_{K^{\mathrm{op}}}H$, naturally in $H$. This is a three-map calculation from the cited statements, not an additional sections theorem being assumed.

source.place: Corollary 3.3.3.4 and its contravariant formulation; agent derivation from the existing classification by the explicit exponential adjunction and cone criterion.

proof.text: Construct the cocone on $h\circ p_F$ coherently. In a larger universe apply the mapping-bifunctor and target-fixed-arrow clauses of [lem-coef-space-transport-classification] to the presheaf quasicategory and the object $F$. Pull back its target-fixed-arrow right fibration along $h:C\to\mathcal P(C)$. It is a right fibration $R_F\to C$ classifying $c\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(h_c,F)$. Step 2 gives a coherent equivalence of this functor with $F$, with small fibers. The mapping-space formula of the same classification represents its inverse by an actual over-map $E_F\to R_F$ over $C$; the representative $R_F$ is allowed to be larger, since its fibers are essentially small. Compose this map with the inclusion into the target-fixed arrow category. By its definition an $n$-simplex is a family of arrows with target $F$, so evaluation gives a simplicial map $E_F\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal P(C)$ restricting at $0$ to $h\circ p_F$ and at $1$ to the constant $F$. This is the required coherent cocone $\alpha:h\circ p_F\to\Delta_{E_F}F$. Its leg at $e=(c,x)$ is the inverse-Yoneda image of $x\in F(c)$. Equivalently, it acts on $a:d\to c$ by $a\mapsto F(a)(x)$, with transport providing the higher simplices. The construction uses the equivalence on spaces of over-maps, not an attempt to assemble independent choices of legs. Enlarging the universe for the arrow category does not enlarge $E_F$: the index was chosen small in step 1.

source.place: Lemmas 5.1.5.2-5.1.5.3: the canonical representable cocone over the category of elements; agent construction in the coherent right-fibration model.

proof.text:
For a test presheaf $G$, an over-map $a:E_F\to E_G$ is exactly a section $e\mapsto(e,a(e))$ of $E_F\times_C E_G\to E_F$. This is a degreewise isomorphism of the corresponding simplicial mapping sets, also on parameters $\Delta^n$. By pullback compatibility in [lem-coef-space-transport-classification], this right fibration classifies $G\circ p_F^{\mathrm{op}}$. Steps 1 and 3 therefore give
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(F,G)\simeq\operatorname{Fun}_{/E_F}(E_F,E_F\times_CE_G)\simeq\lim_{e\in E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}G(p_F(e)).$$
Step 2 also identifies the last diagram, coherently, with $e\mapsto\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(h_{p_F(e)},G)$. Under these identifications the map is precomposition by $\alpha$: an over-map representing $g:F\to G$ sends the element $x$ of $F(c)$ to $g_c(x)$, while $g\alpha_{(c,x)}$ evaluates at $1_c$ to the same $g_c(x)$. The parameter-simplex descriptions prove this identification on the entire mapping spaces, including the compatibility along every simplex of $E_F$. Thus the actual comparison $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(F,G)\to\lim_{E_F^{\mathrm{op}}}\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal P(C)}(h_{p_F(e)},G)$ induced by $\alpha$ is an equivalence for every $G$. This is exactly the colimit mapping-space criterion in [lem-coef-infinity-yoneda-presheaf-limits], so $\alpha$ is colimiting. This proves $F\simeq\operatorname{colim}_{E_F}h\circ p_F$, with all transformations and higher homotopies retained.

lean.statement: theorem space_yoneda_density (C : SSet.{u}) [SSet.Quasicategory C] : (∃ point : infinityCategory.{u} _⦋0⦌, SSet.Enhanced.IsContractible (densitySpaceValue point) ∧ ∀ c : C _⦋0⦌, ∃ t : densityEvaluationElements C c point _⦋0⦌, t.1.1 = densityRepresentable C c ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsInitial (densityEvaluationElements C c point) t ∧ ∃ e : infinityCategory.{u} _⦋1⦌, t.1.2 = SSet.Enhanced.diagramVertex (SSet.yonedaEquiv.symm e) ∧ HEq (densitySpaceEdgeMap e) (SSet.const (X := densitySpaceValue point) (densityIdentity C c))) ∧ (SSet.Enhanced.AreNaturallyEquivalent (densityMappingPairing C) (densityEvaluationPairing C) ∧ DensityCoherentEvaluation C) ∧ (∀ F : infinityPresheaves C _⦋0⦌, ∃ (E : SSet.{u}) (p : E ⟶ C), ∃ t : SSet.Enhanced.coconeCategory (SSet.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}.map p ≫ infinityYoneda C) _⦋0⦌, t.1.1 = F ∧ SSet.Enhanced.IsColimiting (SSet.uliftFunctor.{u + 1, u}.map p ≫ infinityYoneda C) t)
